title: Arrays & Objects
canDo: store and access data in arrays and objects

blocks.md: Every real app manages lists of things — a to-do list, a shopping cart, a feed of posts. JavaScript gives you two tools for that job: **arrays** (ordered lists) and **objects** (named bags of data). Together they let you model almost any real-world dataset, like a list of tasks where each task has a title, a due date, and a done flag.

blocks.canDo: store and access data in arrays and objects
blocks.md: By the end of this session you will be able to create arrays, read and write values by index, add items with `push`, create objects with named properties, access those properties with dot notation, and combine both into an array of objects that models a real list of tasks.

**Arrays** store values in order, starting at index `0`. Create one with `[]`, read with `arr[0]`, add to the end with `arr.push(value)`.

**Objects** store key-value pairs. Create one with `{}`, read a value with `obj.key` (dot notation) or `obj["key"]` (bracket notation). Keys are strings; values can be anything.

**Array of objects** is the pattern that powers real data. Each item in the array is an object — e.g. `[{ title: "Buy milk", done: false }, { title: "Write code", done: true }]`. You iterate with a loop to render, filter, or update each item independently.

blocks.md: **Index starts at 0, not 1.** The first item is always `arr[0]`. Off-by-one errors (trying `arr[1]` for the first item) are the #1 beginner array mistake. When in doubt, `console.log(arr[0])` to check.

questions.question: Given `const fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]`, what does `fruits[1]` return?
questions.explanation: Array indices start at 0, so index 1 is the second element: "banana".

questions.question: Which line correctly adds "mango" to the end of the `fruits` array?
questions.explanation: `push` is the standard method for appending a value to the end of an array. `append` doesn't exist in JavaScript.

questions.question: Given `const task = { title: "Walk dog", done: false }`, how do you read the title?
questions.explanation: Dot notation (`task.title`) is the standard way to access a named property on an object.

blocks.md: You now know how to create arrays with `[]`, read items by index (`arr[0]`), and add items with `push`. You can create objects with `{}` and access properties with dot notation (`obj.key`). Most importantly, you can combine both — an **array of objects** — to model real data like a task list. That pattern is the foundation of almost every UI you'll build.
